title: Mini-sprint latchup: applied-ml catch-up and experiment notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick catch-up after the 4-day mini-sprint (Apr 5–7). This doc is a raw capture: standup highlights, experiment outcomes for 4-bit runs, KV cache observations, onboarding checklist for the new 13B variant, and next-step action items. No polished writeup yet — saving that for a follow-up writeup if we decide to freeze changes.

Attendees (daily rotation):
- Asha P. (owner)
- Marco L. (benching + infra)
- Renee G. (evals + prompting)
- Omar K. (runtime + kv cache)
- Priya D. (onboarding owner)
- occasional: SRE buddies (infra smoke)

Agenda items hit across standups:
1) PTQ 4-bit sweep on 13B-cand-A (FP16 baseline -> 4-bit int8-ish via GPTQ-style PTQ)
2) Eval runs: convo-bench-v2 (50 prompt families), harmfulness quick-check, and instruction-following subset
3) KV cache eviction case seen on long tokens (seq len > 2k) with microbatching enabled
4) Onboarding checklist for customer-facing 13B variant (config, flavors, perf profiles)

Experiments (short notes):
- Experiment Q-13A-ptq-APR7: Applied per-channel symmetric 4-bit quant (outlier-clamp=1.5x).
  - Setup: single A500-80GB, batching off (latency mode), sequence length 512 -> 1024 for tail tests.
  - Baseline throughput (FP16): 45 tokens/sec (p50 latency ~22ms/token).
  - 4-bit PTQ run: throughput 68 tokens/sec (+51%), p50 latency ~14ms/token.
  - Quality: avg EM-like match on convo-bench-v2 down 1.9 percentage points. Instruction-following score (subset) dropped 0.8 pts. Harmfulness delta: no statistical increase in flagged responses on quick-check.
  - Notes: small hallucination patterns on math prompts — likely due to outlier-ranges; need to try outlier-aware bit allocation next.

- Experiment Q-13A-ptq-kv: Same quant config + enabled persistent prefix KV cache across requests
  - Observed: large variance in latency when cache filled past ~1.2M tokens stored keys (~eviction thrash).
  - Root cause hypothesis: current cache eviction policy uses naive LRU per worker; when microbatching is used across concurrent requests there is frequent cross-worker re-keying, causing extra cache updates and pointer churn.
  - Temporary mitigation: increase per-worker cache capacity and adjust eviction to segmented LRU (Marco to prototype).

Eval summary (Renee):
- convo-bench-v2: 50 families x 10 prompts = 500 prompts. 4-bit model: small regression concentrated in arithmetic and token-order-sensitive tasks.
- Instruction subset: behavior preserved for most templates; failures clustered on long-chain reasoning prompts.
- Cost impact: per-token GPU compute cost reduced ~38% on 4-bit quant path (rough calc using p95 utilization numbers).

Onboarding checklist for 13B-cand-A (Priya):
- Configs to produce: perf-profile-low-latency, perf-profile-high-thp, quantized-4bit-profile.
- Required docs: minimal quickstart, fallback-policy example (route to 13B-cand-B FP16), performance expectations table (latency/thp/cost per token).
- Security: confirm KMS key props with infra (ticket created).
- Canary plan: 10% traffic, ramp to 40% over 24h if no ops errors and eval regression <= 2 pts.

KV cache micro-incident log (Omar):
- Apr 6 11:32: intermittent 503s during a microbatch stress test; trace leads to cache invalidations + repeated re-resolve of keys on worker restart.
- Short-term fix: disable cross-worker cache sync path for canary deployments until we validate new eviction policy.

Open technical actions (owners):
- Marco: prototype segmented-LRU eviction and run heavy-concurrency microbatch replay by Apr 12. (JIRA-ML-9015)
- Renee: create a focused prompt-suite for arithmetic + long-chain reasoning to isolate quant failure modes by Apr 11. (linked artifact draft in GH gist)
- Priya: draft onboarding perf-profile docs + sample rollout YAMLs by Apr 14; include fallback examples.
- Omar: instrument per-worker KV metrics (miss/hits/evictions) and add tracing tags to identify cross-worker churn points; finish by Apr 10.
- Asha: coordinate smoke canary with SRE, draft canary SOP and rollback playbook by Apr 13.

Quick wins / experiments to try next sprint:
- hybrid-quant: allocate 6-bit to attention + 4-bit to FF for sensitive layers (Renee + Marco).
- outlier-aware GPTQ variant with per-channel scale-clipping (to target math hallucinations).
- prompt-adaptive caching: larger prefix preservation for instruction-heavy sessions, with capped evict score.

Notes to self / unresolved questions:
- How much perf loss in instruction-following is acceptable for a cost-first SKU? Threshold likely customer-dependent; recommend exposing both FP16 and quantized variants in product.
- Need to formalize the metric that will gate rollout: mixture of convo-bench delta, instruction-following delta, and harmfulness delta. (Proposal: weighted sum with harmfulness having top weight.)
- Is segmented-LRU sufficient under cross-worker microbatching, or do we need epoched cache owner tokens?

Miscellaneous capture (scratch):
- Marco mentioned an oddness when using nvcuvid profiling: one layer shows heavy memcpy between GPU and host in quant path — might be a transient path in kernel selection.
- Priya: request from sales for a quick bench showing 13B quantized cost per 1M tokens for an enterprise deck — add to next slice.
- Small todo: add short-run smoke on dedicated infra (dense gpu pool) vs hosted to compare cross-tenant variance.

Decision log (if anyone asks later):
- For canary: we will not enable cross-worker cache sync on first rollout of 4-bit SKU.
- On quality threshold: soft gate at 2.5 pts convo-bench delta; hard gate at 4 pts. Harmfulness delta must be <= 0.5 pts.

Meeting end note:
This doc is a working capture for the mini-sprint. I expect follow-ups: (1) a short PR with segmented-LRU prototype, (2) a formal eval report with error breakdowns for the 4-bit variant, and (3) onboarding docs + sample canary YAMLs.

-- Asha P.
